transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-24
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Asha Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Carlos Ramirez (CTO - BluePeak), Maya Singh (ML Eng), Priya Rao (Head of Security), Ethan Lowe (DevOps)

--- Optional auto sections (auto-generated):
Summary: Quick console walkthrough focusing on tracing, request logs, and debugging flows for intermittent 502 errors.
Topics: Tracing overview, request logs export, error analysis, RBAC for logs, KMS/encryption, dedicated vs hosted routing for low-latency workloads.
Action items: see metadata list above.

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Asha: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm asha from redwood. we'll kick off, liam and i will run through the console tracing and logs and then leave time for q's.
[00:18] Carlos: thanks, yeah we got the invite. quick context — we started seeing intermittent 502s in our inference path last week, and it's impacting our customer-facing summarization job. we want to understand debugging flow and how we can get visibility.
[00:34] Liam: got it. can you share briefly your setup? dedicated vs hosted, are you on a vpc, things like that.
[00:44] Maya: we're on hosted for now, but plan to move to dedicated in q2 if performance looks good. running a pinned gpt-variant on 8k context, high tokenization, and we've got a small batch pipeline.
[01:05] Ethan: also, we have strict data residency — logs need to be retained in eu-west-1, that's non-negotiable for our customers.
[01:18] Priya: and from security side, we need KMS integration, SOC2 docs, and RBAC for access to request logs.
[01:29] Asha: understood. today we'll show the tracing tab, the error analysis view, how request logs are exported, and then we'll demo reproducing an error using a saved trace.
[01:45] Liam: jumping in — here's the tracing dashboard. (screen share noises) apologies transcription — the UI shows traces grouped by root cause, latency percentiles, and endpoints. you'll see a filter for model, route, and tenant id.
[02:05] [Liam] (screen) so if i click an individual trace, we get a waterfall, timing for token generation, kernel selection, and any fallback events where we switched model variants due to capacity.
[02:25] Maya: hmm i'm not seeing kernel selection labels exactly as our infra names — sometimes transcription has aliasing, is that m-l kernel vs ll kernel?
[02:36] Liam: yeah naming can be a little terse in the UI right now; 'll-kernel' is our lightweight kernel path for quantized runs, 'cuda-opt' is the gpu-optimized path, etc. sorry i should have pointed that out.
[02:50] Carlos: where do we see the raw request payloads? that would help reproduce.
[02:58] Asha: request logs tab — you can search by request id, user id, route, or error code. logs include headers, request body (if retention is enabled), response code, and a link to the full trace.
[03:17] Ethan: is the request body encrypted at rest?
[03:22] Liam: yes, encrypted with customer-managed keys if you enable KMS; otherwise we default to platform-managed. demo: go to settings -> security -> key management. (brief pause) note: if you enable CMK, log exports will be encrypted and key rotation follows your KMS policy.
[03:45] Priya: do we get audit logs for who accessed a request log?
[03:49] Asha: yes, console has audit events; under operations audit you can filter for log access and downloads. we can send the doc for retention policies.
[03:58] [00:04:00] Liam: now the error analysis view — this is handy: it groups errors by signature, shows top stack frames, and provides frequency over time. you can click into a signature to see sample requests that hit that error.
[04:20] Maya: can we annotate traces? for example, mark a trace as 'customer reported' and attach a ticket id?
[04:27] Liam: yep — there's a tagging feature; you can add notes and attach JIRA/issue links. that helps with triage when you're doing a long-running POC.
[04:40] Carlos: about the 502s — we suspect it might be gateway timeouts when our batch size spikes. how would we confirm?
[04:50] Liam: first filter traces by error code 502, then look at the waterfall for any long blocking ops, and examine the request logs for payload size and the sequence length. often you see an increase in token generation time right before the 502.
[05:10] Asha: also, routing policies can cause fallbacks; if a primary node is busy, we switch to a compatible variant — the trace shows a fallback event and reason code.
[05:21] Maya: is fallback automatic even on Hosted? what about dedicated pools?
[05:28] Liam: on Hosted, yes, smart routing is automatic but you can set strict routing if you need to avoid fallbacks. on Dedicated you can pin capacity and avoid cross-tenant routing entirely.
[05:40] Ethan: latency requirements — can we set alerts for p99 > X ms?
[05:45] Asha: yep, console has alerts; you can set per-route SLOs and get webhook notifications. we'll include a quick doc link.
[05:56] [00:06:00] Carlos: okay can you show an example trace with a 502?
[06:02] Liam: sure — loading sample trace now. you can see at 00:01:12 there's a kernel swap, then at 00:01:13 we get a 502. look at the request logs — there was a sudden token spike due to a malformed system prompt in that run.
[06:25] Maya: interesting, so misformatted prompts can drastically change tokenization. do you do automatic prompt sanitization?
[06:33] Liam: we do some heuristics in SDKs but we also surface tokenizer token counts in the trace so you can detect anomalies.
[06:41] Priya: for compliance, if we need to redact parts of the payload before export, is that possible?
[06:48] Asha: yes — export pipelines support scrub rules that remove or hash fields; we can show an example in the security pack.
[06:56] Carlos: how easy is it to stream request logs to our S3 in eu-west-1?
[07:02] Liam: supported — delivery to S3 or GCS with KMS encryption on the bucket side. you can configure delivery in integrations -> exports. there's also a near-real-time streaming option if you need low-latency observability.
[07:20] Ethan: any limits on retention or cost implications?
[07:25] Asha: retention and export frequency affect cost — Optimize will recommend batching and retention windows to balance cost vs observability. we'll include some recommended profiles for high-volume customers.
[07:37] [00:08:00] Maya: about RBAC — can we have a role that can view traces but not download raw payloads?
[07:44] Liam: yes, RBAC is granular: view-traces, download-logs, manage-keys, etc. you can create a role and assign to service accounts.
[07:53] Priya: please add that to the security doc, particularly the audit trail samples.
[07:58] Asha: will do.
[08:02] Carlos: let's talk about reproducing the 502 — what would redwood need to reproduce?
[08:08] Liam: ideally the request id and an anonymized payload; from that we can replay in a staging environment. if you can share 2-3 traces that hit 502, we can triage faster.
[08:19] Carlos: timeline?
[08:21] Liam: SE can triage a single trace within 24-48 hours, deeper kernel-level work might take longer depending on root cause.
[08:31] Maya: also want to see perf benchmarks — what does p99 look like under our token distribution?
[08:36] Asha: we can run a narrow benchmark — liam will propose a workload and we can schedule next week.
[08:42] [00:09:00] Ethan: are there integrations with our existing observability stack, say Datadog?
[08:47] Liam: yes, we have export hooks and can push traces or metrics to Datadog/Splunk; for error-based alerts we can sync.
[08:55] Carlos: competitor question — does OpenAI provide similar trace detail?
[08:59] Asha: in my experience OpenAI doesn't give the same per-token kernel timing and fallback events; Datadog and Sentry do app-level traces but not model-kernel-level detail.
[09:10] Priya: okay security question: if we go private (VPC), do we still get the same console features?
[09:16] Liam: yes, Private includes console access via the private control plane; audit and tracing features are available. on-prem deployments are a slightly different packaging but we maintain feature parity.
[09:28] Maya: is there a way to tag traces as part of a canary rollout?
[09:32] Liam: rollouts tie into tracing — you can label traffic by rollout id and compare error rates side-by-side.
[09:39] [00:10:00] Carlos: ok thanks, can you show the request logs export flow?
[10:03] Liam: (clicks) here under request logs -> exports, you configure destination, choose retention, enable redaction rules. then you can kick off an on-demand export of a filtered selection; exports show status and provide direct download links.
[10:22] Maya: any previews of the exported schema?
[10:25] Liam: yes, exported csv/json includes timestamp, request_id, route, tenant_id, masked_payload, response_code, latency_ms, trace_link. small differences depending on encryption settings.
[10:39] Ethan: for the masked_payload, is the masking deterministic? we want to hash user_ids but keep them consistent across logs.
[10:46] Liam: yes deterministic hashing is supported so the same user_id maps to the same hashed value.
[10:51] Carlos: sweet.
[10:53] [00:11:00] Asha: quick pause — any other questions so far?
[11:00] Priya: how does redwood handle PII in logs, and can we do on-the-fly redaction for streaming?
[11:08] Liam: streaming redaction isn't on by default, but you can enable pipeline transforms for streaming exports — they apply scrub rules before writing to your bucket. we'll include examples in the pack.
[11:20] Maya: okay can we walk through a recent support ticket to see triage notes?
[11:25] Asha: yes i'll show an anonymized ticket. (screen) ticket shows initial error report, traces linked, SE notes about kernel swap, and suggested mitigation: reduce batch size or pin to dedicated pool.
[11:44] Carlos: mitigation sounds straightforward; how much work to try dedicated?
[11:48] Asha: Dedicated requires capacity reservation — we can spin up a trial dedicated pool for a week for POC customers. pricing will be shared.
[11:55] [00:12:00] Ethan: are there SLA guarantees for dedicated?
[12:00] Asha: yes, Dedicated includes SLA targets for uptime and latency tiers — details in the pricing doc.
[12:07] Maya: one more question about instrumentation: can we get kernel-level metrics pushed to our telemetry?
[12:12] Liam: yes, metrics like KV cache hit rate, kernel path usage, sequence length histograms can be exported to your telemetry.
[12:21] Carlos: great.
[12:24] [00:13:00] Asha: wrapping up demo portion — we'll share the security pack and the export walkthrough doc, and liam will follow up to triage the 502 traces.
[13:34] Liam: quick note on reproducing — if you can't share raw payloads, even a pseudonymized version with token counts helps.
[13:45] Maya: we'll try to anonymize and share two traces.
[13:50] Asha: final recap and next steps: 1) Asha send SOC2 + network diagram and RBAC samples; 2) Liam to try replay on shared traces and propose mitigations; 3) schedule a perf benchmark next week; 4) Carlos to confirm budget for dedicated by 2026-04-02.
[14:12] Carlos: all good, thanks.
[14:18] Priya: thanks everyone — please include our security slack channel in follow-up.
[14:24] Asha: will do. thanks all.

End transcript.
